title: Stone Game VI
summary: Alice and Bob play a turn-based game with n stones.
statement: Alice and Bob play a turn-based game with n stones. On each turn, a player removes one stone and scores points based on their personal value for that stone. Alice and Bob have different value arrays. The player with the highest score after all stones are chosen wins; a tie results in a draw. Both players play optimally. Determine the game result: return 1 if Alice wins, -1 if Bob wins, and 0 if the game is a draw.
constraints: Players alternate choosing an unused stone and add only their own value; both play optimally. Return 1, 0, or -1 for Alice, tie, or Bob.
hints: Taking a stone gains your value and denies the opponent theirs, so its combined value determines urgency.
Sort stones by Alice value plus Bob value descending and alternate selections.
Accumulate each player’s own value on their turns, then compare scores.
If two adjacent choices are inverted by combined value, swapping them cannot hurt the player choosing first, giving the greedy order.
editorial: If two adjacent choices are inverted by combined value, swapping them cannot hurt the player choosing first, giving the greedy order.

tests.explanation: Choosing the stone with total value four first lets Alice win.
